standard_prerequisites.name: The integers as a set quotient of N x N
standard_prerequisites.statement: Z is presented as the set quotient of N x N by the relation (a,b) ~ (a',b') iff a + b' = a' + b, and for a set A with an idempotent r : A -> A whose fixed points satisfy the canonical-representative condition the book identifies A/~ with the type of fixed points.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof replaces Z by the retract Sm{x:N x N}(r(x) = x) at source line 1416 and pulls the given data back along the quotient map q (source lines 1418-1425).

standard_prerequisites.name: List-free double induction on N x N and the diagonal case
standard_prerequisites.statement: A family Q : N x N -> Type can be inhabited by recursion on the two arguments separately, the diagonal successor case being the one that is not automatic.
standard_prerequisites.use: The function g is built by double induction with the four clauses g(0,0), g(suc n,0), g(0,suc m) and g(suc n,suc m) (source lines 1428-1434).

standard_prerequisites.name: Transport of data across equalities, and equivalences induced by equal elements of a quotient
standard_prerequisites.statement: Given d : P(z) and a path z = z', transport gives an element of P(z'); and if q(x) = q(x') in the quotient, the induced map between the fibres is an equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: The transport step at source lines 1420-1425 produces d'_0, d'_+ and d'_-, and the equivalence e_{n,m} at source lines 1426-1427 is induced by q(n,m) = q(suc n, suc m).

core_obligations: Replace Z by the equivalent type Sm{x:N x N}(r(x) = x) of fixed points of the idempotent r, and let q : N x N -> Z be the quotient map defined by q(x) = (r(x), i(x)) (source lines 1416-1418).

Transport the three given pieces of data d_0, d_+ and d_- across the appropriate equalities to obtain d'_0 : Q(0,0), d'_+ : Prd{n:N} Q(n,0) -> Q(suc n,0) and d'_- : Prd{n:N} Q(0,n) -> Q(0,suc n), where Q := P o q (source lines 1419-1425).
Derive the equivalence e_{n,m} : Q(n,m) -> Q(suc n, suc m) from q(n,m) = q(suc n, suc m) (source lines 1426-1427).

Define g : Prd{x:N x N} Q(x) by double induction using the four clauses, including the diagonal clause g(suc n, suc m) := e_{n,m}(g(n,m)), and note that this clause is what makes the diagonal case of the quotient descend (source lines 1428-1434).

Use the retraction q o proj1 = idfunc to get Q o proj1 = P and a family of equivalences s : Prd{z:Z} (Q(proj1(z)) ~ P(z)), then set f(z) := s(z, g(proj1(z))) and verify the three required computation rules (source lines 1435-1437).

proof_roadmap.step: Replace Z by the fixed-point retract of the idempotent r and introduce the quotient map q.
Transport the given data to Q := P o q and obtain the diagonal equivalence e_{n,m}.
Build g on all of N x N by double induction, with the diagonal clause using e_{n,m}.
Descend g along proj1 and verify the three computation rules.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.10.12 at source lines 1399-1414, the integer induction principle with its three computation rules, proved at source lines 1415-1438. The proof does not induct on the integers: it first replaces Z by the idempotent retract Sm{x:N x N}(r(x) = x) supplied by the preceding remark (source line 1416), pulls d_0, d_+ and d_- back along the quotient map q to a family Q := P o q (lines 1418-1425), and then has to inhabit Q on all of N x N. The obstruction is the diagonal: it is closed by the fourth clause g(suc n, suc m) := e_{n,m}(g(n,m)) (line 1433), whose equivalence e_{n,m} exists only because q(n,m) = q(suc n, suc m) (lines 1426-1427). The final step needs the retraction property q o proj1 = idfunc to identify Q o proj1 with P and to build the family of equivalences s that defines f (lines 1435-1437). None of this is a routine induction on Z; the transported data and the diagonal clause are what make the three computation rules come out.
